questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Where is the DPT vaccine stored in an ice-lined refrigerator(ILR)?
options: Stored in the lower zone as it is heat sensitive
Stored in the upper zone as it is freeze sensitive
Stored in the upper zone as it is heat sensitive
Stored in the lower zone as it is freeze sensitive
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Stored in the upper zone as it is freeze sensitive

DPT vaccine is freeze sensitive and hence stored in the upper zone of an ice-lined refrigerator(ILR).

ILRs are the main method of vaccine storage in primary health centres. They are an important part of the cold chain and they maintain a temperature of 2 to 8 °C for the storage of vaccines.

They have different temperature zones for different vaccines. The upper zone is for freeze-sensitive vaccines like cholera, hep B, rotavirus(liquid), etc while the lower zone is for heat-sensitive vaccines like OPV, measles, etc. Dial or digital thermometers are used to record temperatures inside an ILR.

Freeze sensitive vaccines

• Cholera
• DTaP-hepatitis B-Hib-IPV (hexavalent)
• DIwP or DTwP-hepatitis B-Hib (pentavalent) Hepatitis B (Hep B)
• Hib (liquid)
• Human papillomavirus (HPV)
• Inactivated poliovirus (IPV)
• Influenza
• Pneumococcal
• Tetanus, DT, Td
• Rotavirus (liquid and freeze-dried)

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: According to biomedical waste management protocols, which of the following colored boxes should the instrument shown below be discarded in?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Blue

The above image shows a dynamic hip screw and it should be discarded in the blue color box.

All metallic body implants except metallic sharps are discarded in the blue box. Metallic sharps (scalpels, blades, needles, etc) are discarded in white or translucent boxes.

Other options:

Option A: White (translucent) containers are puncture-proof and leakproof. It is used for the disposal of waste sharps including metals.

Option C: Yellow containers are lined with yellow non-chlorinated plastic bags. It is used for the disposal of anatomical wastes, discarded medicines, and clinical laboratory waste.

Option D: Red containers are lined with red non-chlorinated bags. Recyclable contaminated waste such as intravenous tubes, catheters, and urine bags are discarded in these containers.

questions.text: The Sparsh campaign was launched to spread awareness about which of the following diseases?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Leprosy

Sparsh Leprosy Awareness Campaign (SLAC) was introduced in 2017 on the occasion of anti-leprosy day (observed on the last Sunday of January) to promote awareness about leprosy.

Objectives of SLAC are to create mass awareness in the community on leprosy, to reduce stigma and discrimination in the community and for early detection of Leprosy cases.

Sapna refers to a local school-going girl who will help to spread awareness in the community.

The other developments under NLEP are:

• Mycobacterium Indicus Prani (MiP) vaccine for multibacillary leprosy patients and their contacts (it is in a project mode).
• Nikusth: A web-based system for the data management of leprosy cases.

Note: Meena is a nine-year-old girl, who is the symbol of UNICEF's Girl Empowerment programme to impart important messages on gender, child rights, education, health and development in the South Asian region.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text:
Match the following patients with the corresponding healthcare programs that can suitably cater to some aspect of their needs.

Column I

1. An adolescent girl who is menstruating and requires suvidha sanitary napkins
2. A pregnant woman in her 2nd trimester needing antenatal care service
3. A poor elderly male destitute requiring a coronary artery bypass graft
4. A woman requiring a cesarean section who has to be transferred to a higher center

Column II

a. Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram

b. Pradhan Mantri Rashtriya Janaushadhi Pariyojana

c. Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan

d. Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 1- b, 2- c, 3- d, 4- a

The correct sequence is 1- b, 2- c, 3- d, and 4- a.

1. An adolescent girl who is menstruating and requires suvidha sanitary napkins - Pradhan Mantri Rashtriya Janaushadhi Pariyojana .Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana provides 'suvidha', a 100% biodegradable sanitary napkin for Rs.1 per pad in Janaushadhi Kendras.

2. A pregnant woman in her 2nd trimester needing antenatal care service - Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan. The Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (PMSMA) ensures quality antenatal care service. With this, a pregnant woman receives at least 1 check-up in her second or third trimester by a doctor in identified public health facilities (PHCs/ CHCs, DHs/ urban health facilities etc). This happens on the 9th of every month. A package of investigations (including one ultrasound during the 2nd trimester of pregnancy) and medicines such as IFA supplements, calcium supplements etc would be provided to all pregnant women attending the PMSMA clinics.

3. A poor elderly male destitute requiring a coronary artery bypass graft  - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana

• Provides a cover of Rs. 5 lakhs per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization across public and private empanelled hospitals
• There is no restriction on the family size, age or gender.
• All pre–existing conditions are covered from day one.
• Cashless access to quality health care services.
• Primitive tribal groups, destitute, and households without shelters are automatically included.

4. Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram- All pregnant women delivering in public health institutions to have absolutely free and no expense delivery, including caesarean section. The entitlements include free drugs and consumables, free diet, free transport from home to the health institutions, between facilities in case of referral, and back home from the health institution. These provisions are for pregnant women and sick infants till 30 days after birth. Other services include free treatment, free drugs and consumables, and free delivery including cesarean section.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 68-year-old man visits your outpatient clinic for a routine follow-up. Which of the following protocols would you use to assess his health literacy?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. SPEAK

The SPEAK protocol is used to assess health literacy in the geriatric population in a clinical setting.

Health literacy is defined as the degree to which individuals have the capacity to obtain, process, and understand basic health information needed to make appropriate health decisions. The SPEAK protocol provides a simple framework that healthcare providers can use to assess literacy. SPEAK stands for:

• S - Speech
• P - Perception
• E - Education
• A - Access
• K - Knowledge

Option A: The GATHER approach is mainly used for counseling (usually, family planning and reproductive counseling) to help people make decisions about health. It stands for:

• G – Greet
• A – Ask
• T – Tell
• H – Help
• E – Explain
• R – Return

Option C: The SPIKES protocol is used to convey distressing information and break bad news in an organized manner to patients and families. It stands for:

• S - Setting
• P - Perception
• I - Invitation or information
• K - Knowledge
• E - Empathy
• S - Summarizing or strategizing.

Option D: The S-BAR technique is used for prompt and appropriate communication among health care workers in hospital settings. It stands for:

• S - Situation
• B - Background
• A - Assessment
• R - Recommendation

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is incorrect about systematic reviews?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Meta-analysis is always performed.

Meta-analysis is not always performed in systematic reviews.

Steps of a Systematic Review:

• A systematic review is the process of locating and synthesizing the research on a particular question using organized, transparent, and replicable procedures.
• It ranks high in the hierarchy of evidence in medicine.

• The research question formulated is always focussed.
• The literature on studies is always found and appraised after criteria of eligibility are established.
• Meta-analysis is usually done in a systematic review but not always.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A patient with Wilm's tumor undergoes renal transplantation. He is currently on corticosteroid therapy to prevent organ rejection. All of the following vaccinations could be given to this patient except?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Intra-nasal Influenza vaccine

Intra-nasal/ nasal spray influenza vaccine is a live attenuated vaccine, therefore it is contraindicated in this patient as he is immunosuppressed.

Live vaccines are prepared from live or wild attenuated organisms. They are repeatedly passed through tissue cultures or chick embryos in the laboratory. With this, they lose their ability to induce full-blown infection in an individual but retain their immunogenicity. It should not be administered to patients with immunodeficiency diseases, lymphoma, leukaemia, or other malignancies. It is also not recommended in individuals on treatment with corticosteroids, antimetabolites, and alkylating agents. Unless the risk of infection exceeds the risk of harm, it is contraindicated in pregnancy.

Live- attenuated influenza vaccine is approved for use in otherwise healthy individuals between age of 2 years and 49 years. Because the risk of transmission of the live-attenuated vaccine virus to immunocompromised individuals is unknown, it should not be used in household members of immunosuppressed individuals, health care workers, or others with close contact with immunosuppressed persons.

Intramuscular influenza vaccine is an inactivated vaccine, which can be given in the immunocompromised.

Other options:

Option A: Diptheria-pertussis-tetanus (DPT) vaccine is a combination toxoid vaccine. The toxins produced by diphtheria and tetanus bacilli are detoxicated and used to prepare the vaccine. They are highly efficacious and safe. The killed whole organism is used for the pertussis component.

Option B: Hepatitis B vaccine is a recombinant vaccine. It is produced by inserting a viral gene segment into a yeast cell. It does not contain viral DNA and will not produce an infection.

Option D: Inactivated polio vaccine is a killed vaccine. As the organism cannot grow in a vaccinated individual, it can be given to an immunodeficient individual.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A statistician is working on a study about the hemoglobin status of children in an area. He plotted the frequency distribution as shown below. Which of the following is most likely to be the mean, median, and mode, respectively of the same?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 11, 9, 7

The image given shows a positively/ right-skewed distribution where mean> median> mode. Hence, the mean, median, and mode must be 11, 9, and 7 respectively. None of the other options have such a sequence.

The observed value that occurs with the greatest frequency is known as the mode. If there are two values that occur with the same greatest frequency, the distribution is bimodal. If there are more than two such values, the distribution becomes multimodal.

When all the values are listed in order, the value that divides the distribution in half is known as the median. When there are an even number of values, the median is obtained by calculating the mean of the two middle scores.

The mean (average) is obtained by summing up all the values and dividing the obtained sum by the total number of values in the distribution.

Skewed distributions are the ones that have asymmetric frequency distributions. They can be identified as positive (right) or negative (left) according to the location of the tail of the curve.

In the image, the tail is located on the positive side of the graph (right side) and so it is a positively or right-skewed distribution. A positively skewed data set contains a large number of low scores but a small number of very high scores. It is vice versa in negatively skewed distributions.

The mean in a positively skewed distribution is pulled up because of the relatively small number of very high scores. The mode is the most frequent and the highest point on the curve, while the median lies between the mean and mode.

Other options:

Option A: Mean= median= mode is seen in a normal (unimodal) distribution.

Option C: Mean< median< mode is seen in a negatively skewed distribution.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Identify this scientist who advanced the germ theory of disease.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Louis Pasteur

The scientist shown in the image is Louis Pasteur.

• Advanced the germ theory of disease; disproved the theory of spontaneous generation.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: What is the best indicator to evaluate obstetric and neonatal care given before and around the time of birth?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Perinatal mortality rate

The best indicator to evaluate obstetric and neonatal care given before and around the time of birth is perinatal mortality rate.

Perinatal mortality includes both late fetal death (stillbirths) and early neonatal deaths. Hence it is a better indicator of obstetric and neonatal care.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text:
Which of the following are considered the best indicators of air pollution?

1. Sulfur dioxide
2. Lead
3. Carbon monoxide
4. Smoke
5. Suspended particles
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 1, 4, and 5

The best indicators for routine monitoring of air pollution are sulfur dioxide, smoke, and suspended particles (1, 4, and 5).

These indicators are monitored daily and their results are reported to a central agency.

Air pollution is the presence of gases and particulate matter in the atmosphere that affect human health and safety. It is also injurious to animals and vegetation. Indicators of air pollution:

• Sulfur dioxide
• Smoke or soiling index
• Grit and dust measurement (suspended particles)
• Co-efficient of haze
• Air pollution index

Air pollution in India is monitored by the National Air Quality Monitoring Program (NAMP). This program is sponsored by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB).

Under the NAMP, four air pollutants are regularly monitored. They are sulfur dioxide (SO2), oxides of nitrogen such as NO2, respirable suspended particulate matter (RSPM/ PM10), and fine particulate matter (PM2.5). Monitoring of meteorological parameters like wind speed and direction, relative humidity, and temperature have also been included with the monitoring of air quality. This monitoring is carried out twice a week.

The health effects of air pollution can be immediate or delayed. Immediate effects include acute bronchitis and suffocation. Delayed adverse effects are carcinoma of the lung and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: All the following are recommendations of Kartar Singh committee except ________.
options: One basic health worker per 10,000 population
Each sub-centre to have one male and one female health worker
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. One basic health worker per 10,000 population

The recommendation of One basic health worker per 10,000 population  was given by Chadah Committee of 1963.

All the other recommendations were given by the Kartar Singh Committee.

Kartar Singh Committee,1973

The Government of India formed a Committee in 1972 known as ''The Committee on Multipurpose Workers under Health and Family Planning" under the Chairmanship of Kartar Singh and the report was submitted in 1973. Its recommendations were

• Recommended male and female health workers
• 1 PHC for 50,000 population
• Each PHC to have 16 sub-centres
• Each sub-centre to have one male and one female health worker

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text:
A hypertensive patient with increased blood pressure has come to the outpatient department. He asks about lifestyle modifications and a DASH diet was suggested. How much does the systolic blood pressure drop by adopting the DASH diet?

DASH: Dietary approaches to stop hypertension
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 8 - 14 mmHg

The systolic blood pressure drops by 8-14 mmHg by adopting the DASH diet.

DASH is a diet plan which involves consuming a diet rich in fruits, vegetables, and low-fat dairy products with reduced saturated and total fat content.

Lifestyle modifications to manage hypertension and the reduction in blood pressure are shown below.

Modification
Impact on SBP

Weight reduction to maintain a normal body mass index
5–20 mmHg per 10  kg weight loss

DASH diet
8–14 mmHg

Sodium intake reduction
(< 6 grams of sodium chloride)

2–8 mmHg

Physical activity: 30 minutes of a brisk walk per day
4–9 mmHg

Limit alcohol consumption
(≤2 drinks/day)
2-4 mmHg

Hypertension is a non-communicable chronic condition that is a risk factor for coronary heart disease, stroke, and other vascular complications. It is known to be an iceberg disease. The rule of halves states that only about half of the hypertensive subjects in the general population are aware of the condition. Only half of those aware are being treated and only half of those being treated are considered to be adequately treated.

Hypertension is a preventable disease. There are two approaches:

• Primary prevention - it includes measures that are taken to reduce the incidence by reducing the risk of onset. Population strategies are dietary modification, weight reduction, and exercise. A high-risk strategy prevents the shooting of blood pressure which might need institutional treatment.
• Secondary prevention - it includes the detection and usage of antihypertensives in affected individuals.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: At PHCs, vaccines are stored in:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Ice lined refrigerators

Ice-lined refrigerators (ILRs) are the main method of vaccine storage in primary health centres (PHCs).

ILRs are an important part of the cold chain and they maintain a temperature of 2 to 8 degree Celsius for storage of vaccines. They have different temperature zones for different vaccines and they are stored accordingly in the baskets that are provided in most ILRs. Dial or digital thermometers are used to record temperatures inside an ILR.

Inside the ILR there is a lining of water containers (ice packs or tubes) fitted all around the walls. When the refrigerator is functioning the water in the containers freezes and cools the cabinet. When the electricity supply fails, then the ice lining maintains the inside temperature of the refrigerator at a safe level for vaccines. Therefore, the temperature is maintained in ILR for a much longer duration than in the deep freezers and domestic refrigerators. Thus ILR is an ideal option for safe storage of vaccines.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A child of 9 years of age is brought to the PHC by his father as he has not received the JE vaccine. All the other vaccinations have been received as per schedule. The father enquires the doctor regarding JE vaccination for his child. Which of the following statements is false about the scenario?
options: A second dose of JE vaccine is given under UIP in the endemic districts
JE vaccine is given via subcutaneous route
Live attenuated vaccine is given under UIP
The JE vaccine cannot be administered under routine immunization in a PHC after 2 years of age.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. The JE vaccine cannot be administered under routine immunization in a PHC after 2 years of age.

The vaccine can be administered to the child as he is eligible to receive the JE vaccine through routine immunisation till 15 years of age.

JE vaccine is administered in the left upper arm subcutaneously.

Note: While administering the live attenuated JE vaccine it is not advisable to clean the injection site with a spirit swab because some of the live components of the vaccine are killed if they come in contact with spirit.

JENVAC is a new inactivated vero cell culture derived JE vaccine produced by Bharath Biotech International limited in India. It is a Kolar strain-derived vaccine. The recommended dose is 0.5ml which is given intramuscularly at left anterolateral aspect of midthigh, 4 weeks apart starting from 1 year of age. Although a booster dose is recommended at a later period, the appropriate time for booster dose administration is not clear.

JEEV is another inactivated vero cell culture derived vaccine from the SA-14-14-2 strain. The recommended dose is:

• 1-3 years: 2 doses of 0.25 ml on 0 and 28 days
• >3years, adolescents, and adults: 2 doses of 0.5ml on 0 and 28 days
• A booster dose of this vaccine is suggested to be given after 12 months of primary vaccination in non-endemic areas.

The inactivated vaccines are currently under the recommendation of IAP. Under the Universal Immunization Programme (UIP), a live attenuated vaccine is given.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text:
Arrange the following in order of the demographic cycle.

1. Early expanding population

2. Declining population

3. Low stationary population

4. Late expanding population

5. High stationary population
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 5, 1, 4, 3, 2

The correct order according to the demographic cycle is high stationary population (5) --> early expanding population  (1) --> late expanding population (4) --> low stationary population (3) -->  declining population  (2).

The demographic cycle has 5 stages:

• Stage 1: High stationary population
• Stage 2: Early expanding population
• Stage 3: Late expanding population
• Stage 4: Low stationary population
• Stage 5: Declining population

In a high stationary population, there is a high birth rate and a high death rate that cancel each other and the population remains stationary.

The early expanding population is marked by a decline in the death rate but the birth rate stays constant. Many countries in South Asia and Africa are in this phase.

In the late expanding population there is a further fall in the death rate, with the birth rate beginning to fall. The population is still increasing due to a net increase in births. India has entered this phase.

A low stationary population is characterized by low birth and low death rate, and this can result in a stationary population. It has occurred in most industrialized countries as a demographic transition shifting from high birth and high death rates to low birth and low death rates.

A declining population is one where the birth rate is lower than the death rate, causing population decline. Examples include East European countries like Germany and Hungary.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: You are a medical officer evaluating the community health meal programs in your area. One of the program's objectives is to attract more children to maintain attendance in school. Which one of the following statements about this meal program is correct?
options: Provides 1/3rd of daily energy requirement and 1/2 of daily protein requirement
Provides 1/3rd of daily energy requirement and 1/4th of daily protein requirement
Provides 1/4th of daily energy requirement and 1/2 of daily protein requirement
Provides 1/2 of daily energy requirement and 1/3rd of daily protein requirement
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Provides 1/3rd of daily energy requirement and 1/2 of daily protein requirement

The correct statement regarding the mid-day meal program is the meal should provide at least 1/3rd of the daily energy requirement and 1/2 of the daily protein requirement.

The mid-day meal program (MDMP)/ school lunch program is catered to provide meals for school children. It is offered to school children in an effort to persuade more children to enroll in schools thereby improving children's literacy. It aims to maintain attendance in schools. Currently, it functions under the broad coverage of the minimum needs program. It is run by the Ministry of Education.

The meal provided under the MDMP should only be a supplement and not a substitute for home diets. It must cover at least 1/2 of the total daily protein requirement and 1/3rd of the total daily energy requirement for children in schools. The cost of meals should be reasonably low. The meals should be easy to cook in schools. Locally available foods must be used whenever possible. The menu should be regularly changed to avoid monotony.

The mid-day meal scheme functions under the ministry of Human Resources Development as a centrally sponsored scheme. Under this, a cooked mid-day meal with at least 300 calories and 8-12 grams of protein is provided to all children of classes I-V.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A female patient visits the OPD with complaints of swelling around her eye as shown in the image. Which of the following transmits the organism responsible for this condition?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Reduviid bug

The sign shown in the image above is Romana’s sign. It is seen in acute Chagas disease which is caused by the flagellate Trypanosoma cruzi. It is transmitted by the Reduviid bug.

The person can become infected if T. cruzi parasites in the bug feces enter the body through mucous membranes or breaks in the skin. The sleeping person may accidentally scratch or rub the feces into the bite wound, eyes, or mouth.

Clinically, the infection course of Chagas disease is divided into acute and chronic phases.

In the acute phase, the majority of the patients will be asymptomatic. Fever, regional lymphadenitis, chagoma (localized subcutaneous nodule at the bite site), and the Romana's sign (unilateral swelling of the eyelids) may be seen.

The chronic phase is characterized by the following findings:

• Chagasic dilated cardiomyopathy with marked bilateral ventricular enlargement. This may lead to congestive heart failure presenting as shortness of breath. Endomyocardial biopsy shows fibrosis and the presence of intracellular parasites.
• Megaesophagus and megacolon.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The new online RNTCP software launched by the government to monitor the TB control programme is called:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. NIKSHAY

Nikshay is a web-based solution for monitoring TB patients.

Nikusth is a web-based solution for monitoring Leprosy patients.

eDOT is an electronic form of DOT to observe patients taking treatment for TB by video. It is an intiative of CDC and currently not available in India.

Nischay is a pregnancy test kit.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A hypertensive patient died from respiratory distress following pneumonia caused by COVID-19(test positive). What should be recorded in line I (c) of the death certificate?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. COVID-19

COVID-19 will be filled in line I (c) of the death certificate, as one of the antecedent causes in the order of the events that took place.

In this patient:

• I(a)- Disease directly leading to death: Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome(ARDS).
• I(b)- Antecedent cause: Pneumonia
• I(c)- Condition which gave rise to antecedent cause: COVID-19

Line II is filled with contributory factors/causes such as diabetes or hypertension.

Other scenarios:

1. In case of pregnancy, puerperium, or birth leading to death in conjunction with COVID-19, record the sequence of events as usual.

For example:

• I(a)- ARDS
• I(b)- Pneumonia
• I(c)- Pregnancy complicated by COVID-19

2. If an HIV patient is dead due to ARDS caused by COVID-19

• I(a)- ARDS
• I(b)- COVID-19
• II- HIV disease

3. Note that COVID-19 patients may die of other diseases or accidents, such cases are not deaths due to COVID-19 and should not be certified as such. In case you think COVID-19 aggravated the consequences of the accident/disease, it may be reported in part II.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text:
Match the following thermometers with their applications.

Type of thermometer
Application

1. Dry bulb thermometer
A. The mean radiant temperature

2. Globe thermometer
B. The cooling capacity of the working environment

3. Wet globe thermometer
C. Low air velocities

4. Kata thermometer
D. The air temperature
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 1-D, 2-A, 3-B, 4-C

The correct match is 1-D, 2-A, 3-B, and 4-C.

A dry bulb thermometer is an ordinary thermometer used to measure the air temperature. It is mounted on the Stevenson screen for accurate readings.

A globe thermometer can be used for the direct measurement of the mean radiant temperature of the surroundings. It is affected by both the air temperature and radiant heat.

A wet globe thermometer is used for measuring environmental heat. It exchanges heat with the surroundings by conduction, convection, evaporation, and radiation. The equilibrium temperature of the globe provides a comprehensive measure of the cooling capacity of the work environment.

A kata thermometer was originally used to measure the cooling power of the air. It was used to assess the indices of thermal comfort. Currently, it is used only as an anemometer to measure low air velocities.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A child was encouraged by his parents to follow a healthy lifestyle to prevent obesity. What level of prevention is adopted in this scenario?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Primordial

Primordial prevention is adopted in this scenario.

The emergence of risk factors for obesity is prevented by encouraging the child to follow a healthy lifestyle from an early age. This reduces the probability of developing obesity in the future.

Primordial prevention is the prevention of the emergence of risk factors in populations in which they have not yet appeared. Most adult health problems have their origins in childhood. Efforts are directed toward discouraging children from adopting harmful lifestyles. The main intervention in primordial prevention is individual and mass education.

Other options:

Option A: Primary prevention is the action taken before the onset of the disease to prevent the possibility that a disease will ever occur. Here, intervention is initiated in the pre-pathogenesis phase of a disease. It is accomplished by population strategy and high-risk strategy. Examples of primary prevention are immunization and sanitizing hands.

Option C: Secondary prevention is halting the progress of a disease which has already occurred. It aims to halt the progress at its incipient (initial) stage and preventing complications. Intervention is initiated in the early pathogenesis phase. Measures like early diagnosis and treatment are used to arrest the disease progression. Examples of secondary prevention are pap smears for early detection of cervical cancer and mammography to pick up breast cancer.

Option D: Tertiary prevention is the action taken to limit impairment and promote rehabilitation of patients in case of irreversible damage. Intervention is done in the late pathogenesis phase. An example is rehabilitation by providing walking aid for the crippled.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: How long does a male worker undergoing sterilization get enhanced sickness benefit at full wages under the ESI act ?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 7 days

Enhanced sickness benefit: Full average daily wage for a duration of up to 7 days in case of vasectomy and up to 14 days in case of tubectomy.

Few important points to be known about the ESI Act:

• It covers all employees getting income up to Rs.21,000/- per month.
• Employer contributes 3.25% of the total wage bill.
• The employee contributes 0.75% of wages.
• State and Central governments share medical expenditure in the ratio of 1:7.
• Medical benefit: Full medical care
• Sickness benefits: 70% of the average daily wages and is payable for 91 days.
• Extended sickness benefit: Payable for up to 2 years for a set of 34 diseases such as TB, leprosy, malignant diseases, diabetes, Parkinson's, Myasthenia Gravis, Glaucoma, Coronary artery disease etc.
• Enhanced sickness benefit: Full average daily wage for a duration of up to 7 days in case of vasectomy and up to 14 days in case of tubectomy.
• Maternity benefit: Benefit is payable at full wages for 26 weeks (6.5 months) for pregnancy, 6 weeks following a miscarriage, and 30 days for sickness arising out of pregnancy.
• Funeral expenses: Cash not exceeding Rs.15,000.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: An epidemiologist plans to conduct a prospective study instead of a retrospective study. Which of the following disadvantages does he aim to eliminate by conducting this study?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Recall bias

Recall bias can be eliminated in a prospective study.

Memory or recall bias: When cases and controls are asked questions about their past history, it may be more likely for the cases to recall the existence of certain events or factors, than the controls who are healthy persons. For example, those who have had a myocardial infarction might be more likely to remember and recall certain habits or events than those who have not. Thus cases may have a different recall of past events than controls.

Prospective studies begin in the present and continue into future. Hence there will be minimal change for recall bias.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: According to the national framework for malaria elimination in India, states were categorized based on ______.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Annual parasite incidence

The annual parasite incidence (API) is used to categorize states/union territories under the national framework for malaria elimination in India.

The national framework for malaria elimination in India was launched in February 2016 with the following goals:

• Eliminate malaria throughout the entire country by 2030
• Maintain malaria-free status in areas where transmission has been interrupted and prevent re-introduction

It uses the annual parasite index to classify states/union territories into four categories.

• Category 0 (Prevention of re-establishment phase): States/union territories with zero cases
• Category 1 (Elimination phase): States/union territories with all their districts having API <1
• Category 2 (pre-elimination phase): States/union territories with API <1, but some of their districts having API≥1
• Category 3 (Intensified control phase): States/union territories with API≥1

API is calculated by the formula: confirmed cases during one year X 1000 / population under surveillance.

Regions with API≥ 2 are considered high-risk areas and are eligible for vector control.

Other options:

Option B: Slide positivity rate is used to describe the percentage of slides positive for the malarial parasite. The type of species is not taken into account.

Option C: Slide falciparum rate is the percentage of slides that are positive for Plasmodium falciparum species.

Option D: Annual blood examination rate is derived by the formula - number of slides examined X 100/ Population. It is considered an index of operational efficiency.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: You conduct a study to determine the association between computer use and visual impairment and get a correlation coefficient of +0.4. Which of the following scattergrams best represents your findings?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 2

In the given clinical scenario having a correlation coefficient of +0.4 shows a positive weak correlation and the scattergram that best represents this finding is graph number 2.

Correlation is used to assess the strength and direction of the association between two variables (such as smoking and lung cancer). The correlation coefficient (denoted by r) is represented by a plus or minus sign, followed by a number (Example: -0.88). The correlation coefficient ranges from -1 to +1.

The numerical indicates the strength of correlation:

• Correlation coefficients greater than ± 0.5 are considered strong and are likely to establish (if positive correlation) or disprove (if negative correlation) the association between two factors.
• Correlation coefficients between 0 and ± 0.5 are regarded as weak.

The sign indicates the direction of the correlation.

• Plus sign (+) suggests that both the variables being studied are positively correlated. This means that the high value of one variable is associated with a high value in another. An example is an association between salt intake and blood pressure readings.
• Minus sign (-) suggests that both the variables being studied are negatively correlated. A high value of one variable such as cigarette consumption is associated with a low value of another variable such as life expectancy.

The relationship between two correlated variables can be represented graphically in the form of a scattergram. Each point represents one observation including both the variables and so would be equal to the sample size.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following parameter is used in the calculation of the pearl index?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Total accidental pregnancy

The parameter used in the calculation of the pearl index is total accidental pregnancies.

Pearl Index:

• The pearl index is defined as the number of failures per 100 woman-years of exposure (HWY).

It can be calculated as follows.

• The total accidental pregnancies must include all pregnancies irrespective of the outcome(live births, still-births or abortions).
• The total months of exposure is obtained by deducting 10 months for full-term deliveries and 4 months for abortion, from the total period under review.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Breastfeeding Week is celebrated in ____.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 1st week of August

• World Breastfeeding Week is celebrated in the 1st week of August.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: What is the correct order of a family cycle?
options: Formation, contraction, complete contraction, extension, complete extension, dissolution
Formation, contraction, extension, complete extension, dissolution, complete contraction
Formation, extension, complete extension, contraction, complete contraction, dissolution
Formation, extension, complete extension, dissolution, contraction, complete contraction
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Formation, extension, complete extension, contraction, complete contraction, dissolution

The order of the family cycle is formation, extension, complete extension, contraction, complete contraction and dissolution.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 7 year old female child visits a PHC along with her mother who came to attend the NCD clinic . The physician advised to start prophylactic iron and folic acid supplementation for the child as per Anemia Mukt Bharat Programme. What is the dose of iron and folic acid given to the child?
options: Monthly, 45 mg elemental iron + 500 mcg folic acid
Weekly, 45 mg elemental iron + 400 mcg of folic acid
Weekly , 60 mg elemental iron + 500 mcg folic acid
Monthly, 60 mg elemental iron + 400 mcg folic acid
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Weekly, 45 mg elemental iron + 400 mcg of folic acid

Under the  Anemia Mukt Bharat Programme,children of 5-9 years of age are prophylactically given 1 iron and folic acid tablet weekly, containing 45mg elemental iron and 400mcg folic acid.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: According to the updated VVM guidelines on the oral Rotavac vaccine , which of the following statements is true?
options: Open vial policy applies to both the old and new products of the Rotavac vaccine
Vaccine Vial Monitor for Rotavac is located on the label of the vaccine vial
Rotavac must be stored at -25°C to -10°C at the district level and 2°C to 8°C at the sub-district level
Vaccine schedule has been changed to a 2-dose schedule at 6 weeks and 10 weeks
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Vaccine Vial Monitor for Rotavac is located on the label of the vaccine vial

Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MOHFW) has updated VVM guidelines on the oral Rotavac vaccine to change the location of the Vaccine Vial Monitor(VVM), which was initially on the cap of the vial, to the label of the vaccine vial.

The open vial policy is applicable only to this new product of the Rotavac vaccine. Implementation of the Open Vial Policy allows the reuse of partially used multi-dose vials of applicable vaccines under the universal immunization policy to prevent wastage of medication.

The vaccine schedule will remain the same, that is a 3-dose schedule at 6 weeks, 10 weeks, and 14 weeks. It is to be stored at -15°C to -25°C  till district stores and then at 2°C to 8°C at the sub-district level.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A sexually active woman who was using barrier contraceptives is planning on switching to DMPA injectables. Which of the following is the correct dosage of this contraceptive?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 150 mg every 3 months

The dosage for injectable depot-medroxyprogesterone acetate (DMPA) is 150 mg every 3 months.

The mechanism of contraception are

• Mainly by preventing ovulation
• Bringing changes in the cervical mucus
• Making the endometrium hostile

An important advantage is that it does not affect lactation. Therefore it is an important contraceptive  during the postpartum period to space pregnancies. The side-effects of DMPA include weight gain, irregular menstrual bleeding and prolonged infertility after its use.

Antara (Injectable contraceptive DMPA) and Chhaya (non harmonal oral contraceptive Centchroman) were recently launched by the Government under its Mission Parivar Vikas.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In a population study, the value of the mean is 200. If the standard deviation is 20, 68% of the population will lie between?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 180- 220

68% of the population will lie between 180- 220.

In a normal distribution curve, 68% of the values lie within the median +/- 1 standard deviation and the mean=median=mode. Since the mean = 200 and the standard deviation = 20:

68% of population will lie between Median +/- 1SD, that is, 200 +/- 20 = 180-220

Similarly:

• 95% of population --- Median+/-2SD, 200+/- 2*20 = 160- 240
• 99% of population --- Median+/-3SD, 200+/- 3*20 = 140- 260

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: According to Sustainable Development Goals, which of the following statement is false ?
options: Reduce the global maternal mortality ratio to less than 70 (per 100,000 live births)
Reduce the neonatal mortality rate to as low as 25 (per 1,000 live births)
End the epidemics of AIDS, tuberculosis, malaria and combat hepatitis
Reduce under-5 mortality to as low as 25 (per 1,000 live births)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Reduce the neonatal mortality rate to as low as 25 (per 1,000 live births)

The statement "Reduce the neonatal mortality rate to as low as 25 (per 1,000 live births)" is false, and the true statement is "Reduce the neonatal mortality rate to as low as 12 (per 1,000 live births)".

SDG (Sustainable Development Goals) comprises 17 goals and 170 targets for Agenda 2030.

• The MDGs came to an end in December 2015 and were replaced by the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
• 17 SDGs take their place and as of 1st January 2016, the SDGs of the 2030 agenda for sustainable development officially came into force.
• The five P's of the new agenda are People, Planet, Prosperity, Peace, and Partnership.

Health is positioned in one comprehensive goal SDG 3.

• Target 3.1: To reduce the global maternal mortality ratio to less than 70 (per 100,000 live births)
• Target 3.2: To reduce neonatal mortality and under-5 mortality by as low as 12 and 25 (per 1,000 live births) respectively.
• Target 3.3: To end the epidemics of AIDS, tuberculosis, malaria, and neglected tropical diseases and combat hepatitis, water-borne diseases, and other communicable diseases.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 3 week old neonate presents to the OPD for the first time. He was born by vaginal delivery at home and has not received any vaccines. Which of the following vaccines would be indicated at this visit, as per the National Immunization Schedule?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. BCG

According to the National Immunization Schedule, BCG should be given at birth or as early as possible upto the age of 1 year.

Other Options:

Option B: Hepatitis B should be given within 24 hours of birth.

Option C: OPV-0 should be given at birth or as early as possible within the first 15 days.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A study was done to assess nutritional status among young children in rural and urban areas. 40 children in rural and 30 children in urban areas were malnourished. Which of the following tests of significance is the most appropriate in this case?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Chi Square test

The most appropriate test of significance, in this case, is the chi-square test. It is used to compare qualitative data between 2 groups with independent measures.

In this question,

• Nutritional status (nourished or malnourished) is a qualitative measure.
• Residence (Urban or rural) is again a qualitative measure.
• Further, only these TWO variables are being compared. Therefore, the chi-square test is the most appropriate test of significance.

The Chi-Square test (χ2) is a non-parametric(non-numeric) test and it is used to test hypotheses in relation to nominal scale data or categorical data.

• It is a test of proportions and associations.
• A Chi-square distribution is usually positively skewed but it approaches a normal distribution as its degrees of freedom increase.
• If the frequency of any of the cells of the categorical table is <5, then Fisher’s exact test can also be used.

Other options:

Option B: The paired t-test compares paired data or pre-intervention and post-intervention data of the same group. If a study were to compare BP in a group of patients before and after treatment, then paired t-test would be used. It is also a test done for quantitative variables.

Option C: Standard error of the mean measures how much discrepancy is likely in a sample's mean compared with the population mean. It is not a test for statistical significance.

Option D: The analysis of variance test (ANOVA) is used to test the difference between means of two or more than two groups. Hence it is used in studies with quantitative data. If a study was done to compare the heights of boys in different classes in a school, ANOVA would be used.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text:
According to the national immunization schedule, what is the dose of vitamin A that should be administered with the first dose of the vaccine shown in the image?

IU- international units
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 1 lakh IU

The image shown below is of the measles-rubella(MR) vaccine. According to the national immunization schedule, 1ml containing 1 lakh IU of vitamin A should be given orally along with the first dose of the measles-rubella vaccine.

The supplementation of vitamin A is summarised as follows:

• A single dose of 100,000 IU is given with measles vaccine at 9 months and
• A single dose of 200,000 IU with the DPT booster at 15-18 months
• A single dose of 200,000 IU every 6 months
• Children with measles and severe malnutrition should receive vitamin A at 1 Lakh IU if <1-year-old and 2 Lakh IU if older.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: An epidemiologist gives a lecture on pandemics. He cites the influenza pandemic as an example of which of the following?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Cyclical trend

The influenza pandemic is an example of a cyclical trend.

A cyclical trend is a type of periodic fluctuation. It occurs in cycles that are spread over short periods of time. This can be days, weeks, months, or even years. Influenza pandemics are known to occur at intervals of 7- 10 years, due to antigenic variations. Some non-infectious conditions can also display cyclical trends. An example of this is road traffic accidents occurring more frequently on the weekends. Knowledge of the cyclical pattern of diseases can be used to protect communities against the same.

Other options:

Option A: Seasonal trend is a type of period fluctuation which refers to seasonal variation of diseases. Examples of diseases that follow this trend include measles, malaria, and upper respiratory tract infections. It can be related to environmental conditions such as temperature and humidity. Some non-infectious conditions which follow this trend are sunstroke, hay fever, and snakebite.

Option B: Secular or long-term trend signifies the changes seen in the occurrence of a disease over a long period of time. It implies a consistent change in a particular direction such as a progressive increase or decrease. Examples of conditions that follow this pattern are coronary heart disease and lung cancer which have shown a consistent upward trend. A decline in the occurrence of diseases such as tuberculosis and diphtheria has been noted in developed countries.

Option C: Point-source epidemic is a type of common-source epidemic. In this type of epidemic, there are no secondary waves and the epidemic curve rises and falls rapidly. There is a clustering of cases within a narrow interval of time. All the cases develop within one incubation period of the specific disease.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A researcher wants to combine twenty different clinical trials to assess the effect of a drug used for Parkinson's disease. Which of the following best explains the type of study conducted?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Meta-analysis

The type of study described here is a meta-analysis that involves combining results from multiple studies on a given topic.

Meta-analysis is the quantitative analysis of the results obtained from a systematic review. A systematic review uses certain inclusion and exclusion criteria to review multiple studies. By combining the results of multiple studies, the power of analysis and generalizability is increased.

Other options

Option A:  A cohort study is a type of analytical study that is done to support or refute an association between a suspected cause and disease. It can be prospective, retrospective, or a combination of the two. The cohorts are selected prior to the appearance of the disease being studied in prospective studies. In retrospective studies, the outcome has already occurred before the start of the study.

Option B: A case-control study is another type of analytical study. It is often called retrospective studies. It is a common method used to test causal hypotheses initially. It proceeds from effect to cause. Both the exposure and outcome have already occurred before the start of the study. It has a control and comparison group.

Option D: A randomized control trial (RCT) is used to evaluate methods of treatment and prevention by scientific techniques. By randomization, the participants are divided into two groups - study and control. The former group receives the procedure or intervention while the latter does. This helps to eliminate bias and ensures comparability.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A newly pregnant woman from a rural area registered in the scheme shown below. Which of the following benefits would she receive under this scheme?
options: At least 4 antenatal checkups and 6 homebased newborn care visits
Free checkup on 9th of every month
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Free checkup on 9th of every month

The above image shows the logo of Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (PMSMA). Under this scheme, all pregnant women will receive a free checkup on the 9th of every month.

Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (PMSMA):

Benefit: Free checkup on the 9th of every month.

Objective: Improve the quality and coverage of antenatal care, diagnostics, and counseling services.

Implementation: Pregnant women receive at least one check-up in their second or third trimester by a doctor in the PMSMA clinic, specifically on the 9th of every month.

After routine examination, pregnant women are categorized according to the risk factors, and different coloured stickers are pasted on mother and child protection cards.

• Green sticker: For women with no detected risk factor
• Red sticker: For women with detected risk factor

Other options:

Option A: Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY):

• Benefit: Cash incentive of 5000 rupees.
• Eligibility: Provided to all pregnant women and lactating mothers for the first living child of the
• family, subject to specific conditions.

Option B: Surakshit Matritva Aashwasan (SUMAN):

• Benefit: At least 4 antenatal checkups and 6 home-based newborn care visits.
• Objective: Assured, dignified, and respectful delivery of quality healthcare services at no cost, aiming to end all preventable maternal and newborn deaths.
• Implementation: Ensures zero tolerance for denial of services to any woman and newborn, providing antenatal checkups and home-based newborn care visits.

Option D: Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY):

• Benefit: Cash incentive of 1400 rupees.
• Eligibility: Provided to all pregnant women who undergo institutional delivery in low-performing states.
• Objective: Promote institutional delivery to reduce maternal and neonatal mortality.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: 4-8 speakers talk about a specific topic in front of a large audience. There is no particular agenda, set speech, or order of speaking. In the end, there is interaction with the audience. What is this mode of communication best known as?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Panel discussion

The given premise best denotes a panel discussion.

In a panel discussion,

• 4 to 8 experts are allowed to have a discussion on a topic in front of an audience.
• No speeches or order is set beforehand.
• A moderator is present to regulate the discussion.
• The audience is invited to speak after the discussion and ask questions.

Methods of Health Communication

Individual approach
Group approach
Mass approach

1. Personal contact
2. Home visits
3. Personal letters

1. Lectures
2. Demonstrations
3. Discussion methods

• Group discussions
• Panel discussion
• Symposium
• Workshop
• Conferences
• Seminars
• Role play

1. TV
2. Radio
3. Newspaper
4. Printed material
5. Direct mailing
6. Posters
7. Health museums
8. Health exhibitions
9. Folk method
10. Internet

Other options:

A symposium is a series of speeches on a selected subject by experts. Each expert presents an aspect of the subject briefly, after which the audience is allowed to ask questions. There is no discussion among symposium members. The chairman makes a comprehensive summary at the end of the session.

A workshop is a series of meetings with an emphasis on individual work within a group, with the use of external consultants or experts. It can be divided into small groups each with a chairman and recorder. Each individual solves a part of the problem and leaves the workshop with a plan of action.

Seminars are similar to conferences and it incorporates a variety of methods like speeches, discussions for health education, and may last for half a day to a week.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: The non-communicable disease (NCD) clinic at the district hospital screens people above the age of 50 years with positive family history for diabetes. What type of screening is this?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. High-risk screening

The non-communicable disease/ NCD clinic at the district hospital screening people above the age of 50 years for diabetes is a type of high-risk screening.

Screening is searching or testing for diseases or defects that are not evident in apparently healthy individuals. High-risk or selective screening is screening applied selectively to high-risk groups defined on the basis of epidemiological research. For example, screening the other members in families of patients with diabetes or hypertension that tend to aggregate in families. It is an effective and economical method of screening.

Other options:

Option A: Mass screening is the screening of a population or a sub-group of the population for a disease irrespective of the particular risk an individual may run of contracting the disease in question. It is not a useful preventive measure unless there is a  suitable treatment that alters the duration or outcome of a disease.

Option B: Multiphasic screening is the application of two or more screening tests (instead of carrying out separate screening tests for a single disease) to a large number of people in the form of health questionnaires, clinical examinations, and investigations. It has not shown any benefit to the population in terms of mortality and morbidity reduction and has instead increased the cost of health services.

Option C: Prospective screening is screening people for the benefit of others. For example, screening immigrants for infectious diseases such as tuberculosis to protect the home population from the disease.

Note: Prescriptive screening is defined as the presumptive screening of patients for unrecognized diseases for their own benefit. It usually does not arise from a patient's request. Examples include screening for bacteriuria in pregnancy and screening for hemolytic disease in a neonate.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: All of the following are duties of a male health worker except?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Maintenance of eligible couple registers

All of the options are duties of male health workers except maintenance of eligible couple registers.

The maintenance of eligible couple registers comes under the purview of the female health workers. She is also expected to regularly update it.

Male health workers are responsible for environmental sanitation. This includes chlorination of public water sources such as wells at regular intervals. They are expected to assist the accredited social health activist (ASHA) and other health volunteers in carrying out directly observed therapy, and short-course (DOTS) activities. He also motivates tuberculosis patients to adhere to regular treatment. They also have duties under the Reproductive and Child Health Program (RCH). This includes the distribution of conventional contraceptives to couples. He also helps prospective sterilization acceptors to undergo the procedure.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 20-day-old infant is struggling to breathe and is unable to feed properly. The mother lacks the financial means to visit the nearest hospital. Which national program offers assistance to help her take the child to a healthcare facility?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Janani shishu suraksha karyakram

The Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram has provisions of free transport from home to the health institutions, between facilities in case of referral and back home from the health institution. These provisions are for:

• Pregnant women
• Sick infants

It includes:

• Free transport
• Free treatment
• Free drugs and consumables
• Free diagnostics and diet
• Free and cashless delivery
• Free C-Section
• Free provision of blood.

Other options:

Option A: Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) is a safe motherhood intervention under the National Health Mission. It is being implemented to reduce maternal and neonatal mortality by promoting institutional delivery among poor pregnant women.

Option B: The LAQSHYA initiative is for improving the quality of labour rooms and providing Respectful Maternity Care. It also includes expanding the obstetric ICUs at government medical college hospitals.

Option D: Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (PMSMA) ensures quality antenatal care service. With this, a pregnant woman receives at least 1 check-up in her second or third trimester by a doctor in identified public health facilities (PHCs/ CHCs, DHs/ urban health facilities etc). This happens on the 9th of every month. A package of investigations (including one ultrasound during the 2nd trimester of pregnancy) and medicines such as IFA supplements, calcium supplements etc would be provided to all pregnant women attending the PMSMA clinics.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: If the sensitivity and specificity of a screening test are 90% and 95% respectively, calculate the positive likelihood ratio:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 18

The positive likelihood ratio of this screening test is 18.

A positive likelihood ratio, or LR+, is the probability that a positive test would be expected in a patient with a disease divided by the probability that a positive test would be expected in a patient without a disease. In other words, an LR+ is the true positivity rate divided by the false positivity rate.

Positive Likelihood Ratio= Sensitivity/(1-Specificity)

LR+= 0.9/1-0.95= 0.9/0.05 = 18.

Similarly , Negative Likelihood Ratio= (1- Sensitivity)/Specificity

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 45-year-old man living in Nellore, Andhra Pradesh presents with the following lesions on his teeth. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Fluorosis

The above image along with the endemic area of Andhra Pradesh is diagnostic of Dental fluorosis.

Dental fluorosis (also termed mottled enamel) is an extremely common disorder, characterized by hypomineralization of tooth enamel caused by ingestion of excessive fluoride during enamel formation.

Fluorosis occurs when drinking water contains excess amounts of fluorine, in the range of 3-5mg/L. It is endemic in parts of India- Andhra Pradesh (Nellore, Nalgonda, Prakasam), Punjab, Haryana, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu.

Mechanism:

• In the extra-cellular environment of maturing enamel, an excess of fluoride ions alters the rate at which enamel matrix proteins (amelogenin) are enzymatically broken down and the rate at which the subsequent breakdown products are removed.
• Fluoride may also indirectly alter the action of protease via a decrease in the availability of free calcium ions in the mineralization environment.
• This results in the formation of enamel with less mineralization.
• This hypomineralized enamel has altered optical properties and appears opaque and lustreless relative to normal enamel.

Classification:

The two main classification systems which are used in the grading of severity of dental fluorosis are Dean’s system and TF system.

Symptoms correspond to levels of fluoride intake:

• Dental fluorosis: (1.5mg/L) Occurs if excess fluoride is ingested during the period of tooth calcification, i.e. in the first 7 years of life. Best seen on the upper incisors and almost exclusively affects only permanent teeth. It causes mottling on dental enamel, the appearance of chalky-white patches on the teeth, and loss of shine in the early stages. The white spots progressively turn yellow and can even become brown-black. The loss of enamel gives a corroded appearance.
• Skeletal fluorosis: (3-6mg/L) Occurs due to the heavy deposition of fluoride in the skeleton. Fluorosis stimulates osteoblastic activity, fluorapatite crystals are laid down in bone and these are usually resistant to secondary osteoclastic resorption. This leads to calcium retention, osteosclerosis, and osteophytosis. Ossification of ligaments and fascial attachments is characteristic.
• Crippling fluorosis: (>10mg/L) Can lead to permanent disability.

Genu valgum and osteoporosis of the lower limb are seen in a newer form of fluorosis in Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh. It is seen in people consuming jawar (sorghum), as it promotes greater retention of ingested fluoride.

Interventions for Fluorosis

• Change the drinking water source with a lower fluoride content (0.5 to 0.8 mg/L). Running surface water contains lower quantities of fluorides than groundwater sources.
• Chemical treatment in a water treatment plant can be moderately expensive. The National Environmental Engineering Research Institute, Nagpur developed a technique for removing fluoride by a chemical treatment called the Nalgonda technique.
• Fluoride supplements should not be prescribed for children who drink fluoridated water.
• The use of fluoride toothpaste in areas of endemic fluorosis is not recommended for children up to 6 years of age

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: An infant was brought to the outpatient department with fever and rash as shown below for the past 2 days. The rash was pleomorphic and first appeared on the trunk. What is the secondary attack rate of this disease?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 70-90 %

The given clinical scenario and the image showing a pleomorphic rash are suggestive of chickenpox or varicella infection. The secondary attack rate of varicella infection is 70-90%.

The secondary attack rate is defined as the probability that disease occurs among susceptible persons following exposure to an infectious person within the range of the incubation period.

Secondary attack rate (SAR) = (Number of exposed or susceptible persons developing the disease within the incubation period x 100)/(Total number of susceptible close contacts). The secondary attack rate measures the communicability of the disease.

Varicella or chickenpox is a highly infectious disease caused by the varicella-zoster virus. The mode of transmission from person to person is by droplet infection or by droplet nuclei. This virus can cross the placental barrier and cause congenital varicella.

The incubation period is usually 14 -16 days. The clinical course can be divided into 2 stages. The pre-eruptive stage is marked by the sudden onset of mild to moderate fever, back pain, shivering, and malaise. The eruptive stage is characterized by a rash that appears on the day of fever. They first appear on the trunk and then on the face, arms, and legs. It advances quickly through all stages of macule, papule, vesicle, and scab. Rash exhibits a characteristic feature called pleomorphism because all the above stages of rash may be seen simultaneously at one time.

Most cases of chickenpox are mild and self-limiting. In children, acyclovir decreases symptoms if taken within 24 hours of the start of the rash, but it has no effect on complication rates, and it is not recommended for individuals with normal immune function.

Chickenpox

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: You are tasked with holding a public service announcement about the benefits of getting vaccinated to a small town of farmers. You want to deliver some statistical data to encourage vaccination. Which of the following is the best way to do so?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Pictogram

Pictograms are a popular method of presenting data among the laity and to those who cannot understand orthodox charts.

Small pictures or symbols are used to present the data. Fractions of the picture can be used to represent numbers smaller than the value of a whole symbol. These can be easily understood by laymen and have a greater impact than complex graphs or charts.
